title: Buer shows no brush discharges occur in high vacuum
place_text: NASA electrostatics lab, Kennedy Space Center

tellings.quote: showing that there's no brush discharges in high vacuum conditions

plain: In a NASA electrostatics lab at the Kennedy Space Center, tests showed "there's no brush discharges in high vacuum conditions," meaning the small sprays of electric sparks that leak off charged objects in air did not appear in near-empty space. Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist who says his team built a working push without propellant, tells Michels this was part of his own work, which matters because it would rule out ordinary sparks as the cause of the force they measured.
